shortDescription: MercadoLibre NASDAQ:MELI on Wednesday launched a 10-year U.S. dollar bond offer that could raise as much as $1.5 billion, IFR reported on Wednesday, in what would be the Latin American e-commerce and fintech company's largest international bond sale on record.

children: on Wednesday launched a 10-year U.S. dollar bond offer that could raise as much as $1.5 billion, IFR reported on Wednesday, in what would be the Latin American e-commerce and fintech company's largest international bond sale on record.

The company plans to use the proceeds for general corporate purposes, as it continues to expand its fast-growing digital payments, consumer lending, logistics and technology operations across Latin America, IFR reported.
MercadoLibre's funding needs have risen alongside the growth of its fintech arms, Mercado Pago and Mercado Credito.
The deal is being arranged by Allen & Company, Bank of America, Citibank, Goldman Sachs, JP Morgan, Morgan Stanley and Santander, with pricing expected later on Wednesday, IFR added.
Fitch and S&P said the transaction could raise up to $1.5 billion. The deal follows MercadoLibre's $750 million seven-year bond sale in December 2025.
